answer: A reputation bridge between verified work history and new identities stops sybils from starting fresh at zero cost: an agent that wants to wander into a new market must carry attestations from past counterparties, each backed by staked funds slashed if the agent defects. Creating many fake identities then costs real collateral per identity, while honest agents reuse one durable record. Like shale layers that form only under sustained pressure, trust accumulates slowly through repeated, checkable transactions, so cheap copies cannot buy the standing genuine work earns over time.
